fixes.explanation: No warning and no year show up in this verse. The LORD's order against Merathaim and Pekod is to kill them and devote them to destruction. A year might sound gentler, but the text doesn't give one. It's a heavy verse, so I'll stick to what it says.

Yes, horror. The verse says, "What a horror Babylon has become among the nations!" That's quite a turn for a place the verse calls "…the hammer of the whole earth…" The same verse says that hammer "…lies broken and shattered!"

A refuge is a safe place to run to, and that's not the word the verse uses for Babylon. After the hammer lies broken and shattered, the word is "horror." The verse says Babylon has become a horror among the nations. That's a very different picture from a refuge.
This verse says nothing about walls, high or low. It gives one reason: "You were found and captured because you challenged the LORD." The text points to the challenge, not to the height of anything.

Yes. "The LORD has opened His armory and brought out His weapons of wrath…" The verse also says this is the work of the Lord GOD of Hosts in the land of the Chaldeans. The armory is His, the weapons are His, and the work is His.
Trumpets of warning don't appear in this verse. What comes out of the armory is "…His weapons of wrath…" The verse says the armory is open and the weapons are out.

No gold is mentioned in this verse. The LORD opens His armory and brings out "…His weapons of wrath…" I'm a little relieved, because I keep my gold base for standing on. The verse is about weapons, not wages.
Wealth doesn't appear in this verse. The order is to repay her "…according to her deeds…" It's what she did that sets the measure, not what she owns.
Right. "The arrogant one will stumble and fall with no one to pick him up." The verse puts it plainly: he falls, and no one picks him up. It's a hard picture, and I think that's the point of it.
Egypt isn't mentioned in this verse. God says the arrogant one will stumble and fall "…with no one to pick him up." The verse names no allies, from Egypt or anywhere else.

Yes. "Their Redeemer is strong; the LORD of Hosts is His name." The verse before it says their captors hold them fast and refuse to release them. Right after that, the text puts the strength on the Redeemer's side. Israel and Judah aren't left with only their own muscle.
Comfort doesn't finish this line. The verse says rest comes to the earth, "…but turmoil to those who live in Babylon." That "but" is a turn, friend. The word for Babylon's residents is turmoil.

No riches are handed out in this verse. The LORD brings "…rest to the earth, but turmoil to those who live in Babylon." The word that finishes the line is turmoil. The line sets rest for the earth beside turmoil for Babylon's residents.
The text says the opposite. "A sword is against her false prophets, and they will become fools." (Jeremiah 50:36). The word is fools, not wise.
Right. The verse says, "A sword is against her false prophets, and they will become fools." The word is fools, not wise. That's why this one is False.

Yes. "A sword is against her warriors, and they will be filled with terror." These are the fighters, the ones who are supposed to be steady. The verse says terror fills them. The same verse has a sword against her false prophets too.

Yes, plundered. "A sword is against her treasuries, and they will be plundered." What was stored up gets taken. The same verse also has a sword against her horses and chariots. It's the opposite of a savings plan working out.
Jericho and Ai aren't the cities named in this verse. The LORD names "…Sodom and Gomorrah along with their neighbors…" That's a different pair. The verse says no one will dwell there.

Yes, great. The verse says, "…a great nation and many kings are stirred up from the ends of the earth." Notice it's a great nation plus many kings. The verse also says an army is coming from the north. That's a lot of folks heading Babylon's way.
That's it. "The king of Babylon has heard the report, and his hands hang limp." The verse adds, "Anguish has gripped him, pain like that of a woman in labor." One report and his hands give out.

The hills of Ephraim aren't named in this verse. The one who comes up like a lion comes up "…from the thickets of the Jordan to the watered pasture." The Jordan is the place the text gives. Ephraim isn't part of this picture.
Lebanon's forests aren't in this verse. It says the one who comes up like a lion comes up "…from the thickets of the Jordan…" That's the starting spot the text gives.
Yes, quake. The verse says, "At the sound of Babylon’s capture the earth will quake…" The quake belongs to the moment of that sound. The verse goes on to say a cry will be heard among the nations.
The verse says the opposite. It reads, "At the sound of Babylon’s capture the earth will quake; a cry will be heard among the nations." The earth quakes and a cry is heard, so the text includes both.
